title: Sort by height, turntable
summary: Tell boxes of three heights apart with a light array, and turn a turntable so that each box leaves on the belt of its class.
scope: Passing means your program behaved correctly in the simulator on this computer. It says nothing about a real machine, its timing or its safety, and it does not show the accuracy of the array or turntable speed.
objectives: Tell boxes of three heights apart with a light array that reports a height only while a box is in it.
Make a turntable work with the box it turns, so that each box leaves on the belt of its class.

stages.title: Objective
stages.body: In src/HeightSort.st, run the belts after Start and sort seven boxes by height: a box of about 20 cm must leave on the centre belt, a box of about 30 cm on the belt to the right and a box of about 40 cm on the belt to the left, and none may be dropped. Done must light when seven boxes are sorted.
stages.checkpoint: Short boxes leave on the centre belt, medium to the right, tall to the left, and Done lights after seven boxes.

stages.title: Predict
stages.body: Before running, say what HeightCm reads before a box, while it crosses the array and after it, and which values boxes of 20, 30 and 40 cm give. If the program looked at one scan only, in which scans could it tell the height of a box?
stages.checkpoint: HeightCm reads 0 with no box in the array and 20, 30 or 40 while a box of that height crosses it, so only the scans during the crossing tell the height.

stages.title: Edit
stages.body: Write the program, save it, then press {{ui:learn.check}}. The starting program drives no output, so no belt moves and no box is sorted. After Start the belts must run and each box must leave on the belt of its class.
stages.checkpoint: Check reports the scenario of this lesson as passed.

stages.title: Run
stages.body: Press {{ui:learn.check}}. ZPLC runs your saved program against the scenario of this lesson, with the plant answering your outputs, and lists every assertion that failed. To watch the machine move, press {{ui:toolbar.run.label}} (F5) and open the {{ui:plant.panel.view3d}}.
stages.checkpoint: The required scenario is named height-sorting-turntable and contains {{assertions}} assertions.

stages.title: Observe
stages.body: Watch the {{ui:plant.panel.view3d}} and the trace of HeightCm: it shows the height of a box only while the box is in the array, and 0 otherwise. Watch which way the table faces for each class of box.
stages.checkpoint: A short box never makes the table turn; a medium box makes it face right and a tall box makes it face left.

stages.title: Reflect
stages.body: The grade cannot compare numbers: it sees the bins, not the values your program measured. Any way of telling the three heights apart that sends every box to its own belt gives the same grade.
stages.checkpoint: A box on the wrong belt fails the ALWAYS assertion.

hints.text: HeightCm is 0 whenever no box is in the array, and the box is not yet at the turntable when it leaves the array: what must your program remember about a box, and from when to when?

Latch Start into Active and run RunIn, RunCentre, RunRight and RunLeft while Active. Use an R_TRIG on ArrayBusy to reset Peak to 0, update Peak with HeightCm while ArrayBusy is TRUE, and an F_TRIG to classify into Cls: Peak > 35.0 tall (2), Peak > 25.0 medium (1), otherwise short (0). Then handle one box at a time with an INT State: 1, when AtBlade and AtCentre have been TRUE for 0.3 s, copy Cls into Route so the next measurement cannot change it; 2, lower the blade (Hold FALSE) and run RunTable until OnTable; 3, stop RunTable and wait 0.8 s; 4, set ToRight for Route 1 or ToLeft for Route 2 and wait until AtCentre, AtLeft or AtRight has been TRUE for 0.2 s; 5, run RunTable until OnTable falls; 6, wait 0.7 s; 7, clear ToLeft and ToRight, wait for AtCentre, add one to Sorted and go back to 1. Hold := Active AND State <> 2; Done := Sorted >= 7; Busy := Active AND NOT Done.

faultCases: The starting program drives no output, so no belt moves and no box is sorted.
